text:
Marcus Reed: trying to close on the “canonical prompt shapes” for the perf canary. we keep bouncing between “match real customer distros” vs “keep it synthetic + stable”. can we decide what we mean by canonical per model family?

Noah Patel: canonical should mean: (1) stable enough for p95 deltas, (2) exercises the kernels/scheduler in the way customers trigger them. we can’t chase full distro in v1.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. if we try to mirror customer distribution we’ll end up with constant drift. canary needs to be a measuring instrument, not a mirror.

Marcus Reed: ok but if we go too synthetic (like fixed 256/256) we might miss regressions that only show up at long prefill or weird decode ratios.

Hiro Tanaka: kernel perf cliffs depend a lot on context length + attention pattern. the “interesting” regimes for us are:
- short prefill + long decode (chatty)
- long prefill + short decode (RAG / summarization)
- long prefill + long-ish decode (worst case)
we can pick a small set that spans those.

Nadia Rahman: from metrics POV, fewer shapes = easier to keep labels under control. also baseline noise drops when the request sizes aren’t flapping.

Omar El-Sayed: reminder: the runtime tags we’re emitting for canary are `prompt_tokens`, `max_new_tokens`, and we can bucket them into a small enum like `shape=S1|S2|S3` in telemetry. if we allow “freeform lengths” it’s going to explode.

Marcus Reed: what if we define shapes as token buckets, not exact. ex: prefill 200-300, decode 100-150. but then you still get variance.

Sofia Ivanova: variance matters *a lot* for tokens/sec since batching changes. if you allow a range, the microbatch composition changes run-to-run.

Julian Moore: also for scheduler attribution: we want to pin scheduler mode + keep arrival pattern consistent. otherwise queue metrics are different and we’ll argue about whether it’s the workload.

Noah Patel: proposal: define 3 shapes per model family, exact token counts. plus one “stretch” shape for long-context models. and we can revisit later with a second suite that’s “representative”.

Marcus Reed: per model family meaning like llama-ish vs mixtral-ish? or chat vs instruct?

Hiro Tanaka: more like architecture constraints:
- dense decoder-only (llama/mistral/qwen)
- MoE (mixtral)
- long-context variants (same but 8k/32k)
we can reuse shapes across dense, but MoE might want a separate shape because routing overhead interacts with batch size.

Logan Wright: telemetry note: if we add `model_family` as a label we should make it low-cardinality and controlled (enum), not derived from model name string.

Allison Grant: and please keep “canonical shapes” written down as an explicit spec. we’ll get asked “why these” in every review.

Thomas Baird: cardinality budget: if you ship labels {model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode, shape, stream} we’re already tight. avoid anything else.

Marcus Reed: ok, concrete candidates. for dense models (llama/mistral/qwen):
S1: prefill=256 decode=128 (non-stream)
S2: prefill=1024 decode=256 (stream)
S3: prefill=4096 decode=64 (non-stream)
then maybe S4: prefill=8192 decode=128 for longctx models only.

Sofia Ivanova: why S2 streaming only?

Marcus Reed: because streaming has that first-token timestamp + steady-state decode pacing. we had that tokens/sec bug earlier. i want at least one streaming shape always.

Nadia Rahman: can we do streaming on S1 instead? streaming on 1024/256 might make p95 latency super sensitive to network jitter. smaller is safer.

Omar El-Sayed: streaming path measures (TTFT + per-token) differently, yes. but we can configure the runner to record server-side timestamps only (no client RTT). still, bigger prefill will push TTFT.

Noah Patel: for canary we should measure server-side only. if we’re worried about jitter, add a note in the runner: keep connections warm + same region.

Julian Moore: from scheduler view, S3 (4096/64) is the one that tends to shift prefill-heavy batches. good to have.

Hiro Tanaka: also, 4096 prefill triggers different kernel choices and kv cache behavior. if a regression only shows up there, that’s exactly what we want.

Sofia Ivanova: but if we include 4096 prefill on every model, on smaller GPUs we may end up with different batch sizes / OOM guardrails, which makes tokens/sec not comparable.

Hiro Tanaka: that’s fine as long as we slice by `gpu_sku` and baseline within the slice. canonical != identical throughput, it’s stable within slice.

Thomas Baird: slicing by gpu_sku is already planned, just don’t add “batch_size” as a label. emit batch stats as logs / exemplars.

Logan Wright: +1. we can store batch stats in traces (span attrs) and sample those.

Marcus Reed: question: should we pick token counts from real customer percentiles? i pulled a quick histogram from last month: huge mass at ~200-600 in, 100-300 out. long tail to 8k/1k but tiny.

Noah Patel: use the histogram to justify the shapes, but do not try to match the weights. we’re not doing a Monte Carlo simulator.

Allison Grant: suggest we document it as: “we choose representative *regimes*, not exact distribution.”

Sofia Ivanova: i’m still worried about S4 (8192/128). that’s going to be noisy (cache warming, page faults, etc.). maybe keep it off by default and enable per-region when stable.

Marcus Reed: what if S4 is “weekly” not “continuous”? like a separate cron run.

Nadia Rahman: careful: if it’s not continuous, baseline logic gets weird. but we *can* make it a separate detector with longer window and ticket-only.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. if S4 is low frequency, alert should be non-paging.

Hiro Tanaka: ok. so v1 continuous suite = S1/S2/S3. optional extended = S4 ticket-only.

Julian Moore: can we also fix sampling params? `temperature=0`, `top_p=1`, no tool calls, no JSON schema. anything that changes decode path adds variance.

Marcus Reed: yep. i’ll lock it: temperature=0, top_p=1, repetition_penalty=1.0. also fixed stop tokens so decode length is deterministic.

Sofia Ivanova: and *no* multi-turn chat that grows across requests. each canary request should be self-contained or you’ll get cache effects / prompt growth.

Marcus Reed: ack. i’ll use a single-turn chat template for instruct/chat models. static text, no customer data.

Allison Grant: can you paste the final shape definitions in the design doc + the sheet? reviewers will want both.

Marcus Reed: draft YAML for the runner config (names are stable enums):
```yaml
shapes:
  - name: S1_short
    prompt_tokens: 256
    max_new_tokens: 128
    stream: true
  - name: S2_mid
    prompt_tokens: 1024
    max_new_tokens: 256
    stream: false
  - name: S3_longprefill
    prompt_tokens: 4096
    max_new_tokens: 64
    stream: false
extended_shapes:
  - name: S4_longctx
    prompt_tokens: 8192
    max_new_tokens: 128
    stream: false
    alerting: ticket_only
```

Nadia Rahman: swap stream flag? i’d rather have streaming on S1 (less variance) and non-stream on S2.

Omar El-Sayed: i agree w/ Nadia. streaming on mid-size adds a ton of variance in TTFT because prefill dominates.

Noah Patel: consensus: streaming = S1. non-streaming = S2 + S3. S4 optional.

Marcus Reed: cool. will update config + add a note: S1 streaming is primarily to cover streaming codepaths + TTFT correctness. S2/S3 to cover throughput kernels.

Hiro Tanaka: :thumbsup: please also add a sentence about why 4096 is chosen (kernel selection boundary + kv cache pressure).

Sofia Ivanova: and add “canonical shapes are fixed, changes require ADR/update + baseline reset” so we don’t churn.

Logan Wright: once the names are final, i’ll make sure telemetry buckets `shape` as enum, not raw token numbers.

Thomas Baird: :thumbsup: thanks. that keeps us within budget.

Marcus Reed: ok action items:
- Marcus: update workload matrix + config w/ S1 streaming, S2/S3 non-stream, S4 ticket-only
- Allison: add to standards page as canonical shapes v1
- Logan/Nadia: confirm label schema uses `shape` enum

Noah Patel: works. ship it before we start phase 1 rollout so we can baseline early.

Marcus Reed: done, will push a PR today and link here.
